data.body:
CLOSE ATTEMPT - the plan-review blocker is CLEARED, a completion-verifier blocker remains. Ticket stays in_progress; not forced.

WHAT WAS FIXED. The close was failing with 'plan-review close gate: stale-material: the plan was materially edited since review - changed: description (4392 -> 8980 chars)'. During implementation two long sections ('Companion-ticket status, corrected' and 'Code-reading corrections') had been appended to the DESCRIPTION, and re-reviewing was itself impossible: 8980 chars exceeds the 8000-char plan-review admission cap, so review-plan would have blocked unread on criterion P4. The description was condensed to 6412 chars keeping all substance (P4 then reported desc_chars 6389, limit 8000, pass), review-plan re-ran and returned PASS with 0 blocking and 1 advisory (P6 ac-quality: three criteria bundle deliverables with 'and'; the AC1 grep asserts nothing - deferred at priority 0.40 against a 0.95 block line). The first run's attestation failed to persist ('plan review generation remained unstable after 3 attempts' - the ticket generation moved under the lock, a concurrent-write race on a busy store, not a verdict problem); 'rebar sign-review 4329-4761-6e3d-41d7' re-signed from the recorded sidecar with no LLM re-run, and 'review-plan --status' now reports verdict=certified at e5ef7fe18c9aafdca7ef1f687f9302b0479b91ab.

WHAT NOW BLOCKS. The completion verifier fails one criterion, and the finding is CORRECT on independent check:

  AC2 'Every edge in the table is exercised by the same test for both claim and transition; checked by a parametrised test over the table.'

There is no parametrised test over _CASCADING_EDGES anywhere in the tree. 'grep -n parametrize' returns nothing in either tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_claim_transition_parent_cascade.py or tests/unit/commands/test_lifecycle_cascade.py, and repo-wide 'grep -rn parametrize tests/ | grep -i cascad' is empty; only those two files plus tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_inbound_status_cascade.py mention _CASCADING_EDGES at all. What the suite actually has is one hand-written test per (edge, surface): test_claim_child_claims_open_parent_first, test_transition_child_to_in_progress_cascades_to_open_parent, test_reopen_child_reopens_closed_parent, test_reactivate_child_reactivates_closed_parent, and so on - 32 tests, all green, but enumerated by hand rather than driven from the table. test_the_cascading_edge_table_is_unchanged pins the table's CONTENT (the three edges, and that ('in_progress','closed') is absent); it does not iterate it.

The distinction the criterion is buying is real, not pedantic: a hand-enumerated suite does not fail when a FOURTH row is added to _CASCADING_EDGES, so the next 'an edge the cascade did not know about' bug - the class that produced cranial-sulfur-peafowl and paragonite-fruited-minnow - can still land silently. A test driven from the table cannot miss a new row.

Note also that the criterion is not literally satisfiable as phrased: claim only ever walks the (open -> in_progress) edge, so 'every edge ... for both claim and transition' cannot hold for the two closed-source edges. Any remediation should re-word it as well as build it - e.g. parametrise over _CASCADING_EDGES.items() asserting transition cascades on every row, plus the claim surface on the one row claim supports.

REMEDIATION: add a test parametrised over _CASCADING_EDGES (a new patchset on a stacked change, or its own follow-up), re-word AC2 to match what claim can actually do, then re-verify and close. The plan-review side needs nothing further - its attestation is certified and current.

SIBLING NOTE: the same shape of gap sits on story scattered-bleakish-millipede (111a) - its AC1 names a construct-uniqueness guard test that was never landed. Both are the parent epic airborne-wellloved-kingfisher's durability guarantee going unbuilt while the consolidation itself landed correctly.
